written.description: Judges an MCP server's tool definitions three ways, by YARA rule, by hosted inspection API and by asking a model, so a poisoned tool description has to clear more than one kind of reader.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(examples): port stdio_example.py to the mcp 2.x low-level Server API (#291)

* fix(examples): port stdio_example.py to the mcp 2.x low-level Server API

pyproject requires mcp>=2.0.0, and the other six example servers already
use MCPServer. stdio_example.py still used @server.list_tools() and
@server.call_tool(), which the mcp 2.x low-level Server no longer has, so
the module failed with an AttributeError on import. Pass the handlers to
Server(on_list_tools=..., on_call_tool=...) and return ListToolsResult /
CallToolResult; the tool list and responses are unchanged.

* fix(examples): return tool exceptions as an error result, as the v1 decorator did

* fix(examples): validate stdio example arguments against the tool schema; add a test

The v1 @server.call_tool() decorator checked arguments against the tool's
inputSchema before the handler ran. Restore that, so innocent_calculator with
a="x", b="y" returns an error result instead of "Result: xy".

tests/test_stdio_example_server.py imports the example, so the AttributeError
at import on mcp 2.x can't come back unnoticed, and covers a valid call, a
schema-invalid call and a tool exception.
